newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece plans 15 percent tax on gains on derivatives.
newsitem.headline: Greece plans 15 percent tax on gains on derivatives.

text.p: Greece plans to introduce a 15 percent tax on income and gains from derivatives, trading in currency and interest rate swaps, forward rate agreements and options, according to a new draft bill.
Deputy Finance minister George Drys has prepared a draft bill which, according to news reports, has the backing of the Bank of Greece and the Union of Hellenic Banks.

The bill, expected to be submitted to parliament soon, states that gains from derivatives trades will be subject to a 15 percent witholding tax for individual, corporate and institutional investors. The tax will be the only tax liability on income or gains realised on these transactions.
According to the bill, trades between credit institutions and non-Greek residents will be excluded from the tax.
Dealers said the derivatives market in Greece was just starting to pick up.
The tax would impose an extra cost on efforts to shield investments from currency or interest rate risks, one dealer said.
